title: Distributional value gradients for stochastic environments
claim: A sample-based method couples a learned stochastic world model with a distributional critic and a distribution-matching loss, trained end to end.
layout: 2 panels: block diagram left, code listing right; dashed gradient arrows
description: The left panel is a block diagram of the training algorithm. Colored boxes are the modules: a brown policy network, a pink critic network Z_phi, a pink target critic, a brown target policy, and a blue prior and green decoder grouped inside a boxed 'World model (cVAE)'. Black arrows carry the state s, the action a, noise ξ, and the predicted next state and reward (ŝ', r̂). A discount γ multiplier and a summation node feed a 'Maximum Mean Discrepancy Loss' box. Dotted pink and brown arrows show gradient flow back to the critic and policy. Equations for the policy objective and the cVAE loss are written around the boxes. The right panel is a syntax-highlighted Python pseudocode listing, sample_ms_mmd, with commented steps that compute the biased MSMMD.
caption: Left: block diagram of our DSDPG algorithm, where the critic \(Z_\phi\) maps noise \(\xi\) and \((s,a)\) to Sobolev‐return samples, a cVAE world model generates next‐state–reward samples \((\hat s',\hat r)\), MSMMD or MMD compares predicted and bootstrapped Sobolev‐return distributions, and the policy is updated via the critic’s mean (gradient flows shown as dashed arrows; inspired by [ref]). Right: pseudocode for estimating the biased MSMMD between predicted and bootstrapped Sobolev returns.
abstract: Gradient-regularized value learning methods improve sample efficiency by leveraging learned models of transition dynamics and rewards to estimate return gradients. However, existing approaches, such as MAGE, struggle in stochastic or noisy environments, limiting their applicability. In this work, we address these limitations by extending distributional reinforcement learning on continuous state-action spaces to model not only the distribution over scalar state-action value functions but also over their gradients. We refer to this approach as Distributional Sobolev Training. Inspired by Stochastic Value Gradients (SVG), our method utilizes a one-step world model of reward and transition distributions implemented via a conditional Variational Autoencoder (cVAE). The proposed framework is sample-based and employs Max-sliced Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MSMMD) to instantiate the distributional Bellman operator. We prove that the Sobolev-augmented Bellman operator is a contraction with a unique fixed point, and highlight a fundamental smoothness trade-off underlying contraction in gradient-aware RL. To validate our method, we first showcase its effectiveness on a simple stochastic reinforcement learning toy problem, then benchmark its performance on several MuJoCo environments.
